newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to be alert during surgery.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to be alert during surgery.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will be alert under a local anesthetic during planned surgery later on Friday to repair a torn tendon in his upper right thigh after an early-morning slip, the White House said.
"He won't go under (a general anesthetic)," Mary Ellen Glynn, a White House spokeswoman, said from West Palm Beach, Florida, where the president hurt himself. "He'll be alert the whole time."

Glynn, speaking on the ABC program "Good Morning America," said Clinton probably would need crutches to get around for a few weeks after surgery. She said the surgery would not require a temporary transfer of power to Vice President Al Gore.
The surgery was to take place at Bethesda Naval Hospital when he returns from Florida where he was on a fundraising visit on Thursday.
Asked whether Clinton would go ahead with a scheduled summit in Helsinki on March 19 with Russian President Boris Yeltsin, she said: "There are no plans at this time to change his agenda."
